profile.headline: Senior Software Engineer at Google
profile.summary:
I’ve always been a technical "swiss-army knife" driven by a simple mission: building engineering solutions that genuinely help people. Today, that means working at the intersection of large-scale backend infrastructure and AI data integrity.

I am incredibly optimistic about AI’s potential to transform the world and lift up marginalized communities, but I balance that idealism with a healthy dose of pragmatic skepticism. Real progress requires rigorous safeguards. 

Let's design, optimize, and stress-test intelligent systems to ensure they are accurate, resilient, and change the world together!

positions.title: Senior Software Engineer
positions.description:
I’m an AI-fluent backend serving and infrastructure engineer working on Google Search, focusing on the core features that power high-leverage user experiences. Day-to-day, I build end-to-end solutions that keep global-scale search reliable, fast, and stable, which usually means spending a lot of time on backend optimization, framework migrations, and system monitoring.

Because Search handles highly visible, trust-sensitive topics, a huge part of my role focuses on data integrity and system quality. I specialize in the foundational plumbing that keeps search results trustworthy, working on everything from query understanding and ranking logic to automated error detection, experimentation, and adversarial testing (red-teaming). 

I deliver high-impact solutions that are fair, accurate, and resilient under pressure.

positions.title: Staff Engineer
positions.description:
I spent my time at Stryker in their highly regulated medical robotics division, where I advanced from a contract role through two promotions to Staff Software Engineer in 21 months. As a versatile generalist on a core 6-engineer launch team, I took hands-on technical ownership of the safety-critical bone resection module for the TKA 2.0 surgical application. My main focus was translating existing 3D algorithmic models into validated, production-ready code for robotic saw execution.

Beyond core feature delivery, I specialized in last-mile quality assurance. I used deep root-cause analysis to track down and resolve complex software anomalies, ensuring the final product fully conformed to 21 CFR Part 820 and ISO 13485 legal mandates before deployment. I also bridged the gap between legacy systems and future-state architecture by writing the code that physically executed a core infrastructure migration away from Tcl/Tk frameworks, all while designing the technical onboarding pipeline to help new engineers ramp up quickly.

positions.title: Contract Software Engineer
positions.description: Application software developer for robotic assisted surgery

positions.title: Contract Software Engineer
positions.description:
At TII, I focused on computer vision and biomedical image processing, specifically designing the framework for an automated segmentation algorithm used on OCT images. I took a modular, object-oriented approach to the architecture, prioritizing user-configurability so the pipeline could adapt easily to different parameters.

Beyond hands-on development, I contributed to the technical positioning and documentation for an NIH Small Business Innovation Research (SBIR) grant proposal to help secure funding for the project. Throughout the lifecycle, I collaborated closely with a remote engineering team, managing tasks, documentation, and sprints using Jira and Confluence to keep development moving forward smoothly.

positions.title: Graduate Teaching Assistant
positions.description:
* Received the Outstanding Teaching Assistant Award
* Supervised lab sessions, evaluated performance metrics, and conducted individual mentorship for three distinct academic tiers:
  + Introduction to Biomedical Engineering: Coordinated instruction and programmatic onboarding for 94 freshman undergraduates.
  + Biomedical Measurements & Instrumentation: Implemented an optimized teaching methodology and standardized grading rubric for 27 junior undergraduates, designing and delivering an original workshop on scientific lab report composition.
  + Biomedical Instrumentation: Redesigned and modernized curriculum material for 36 upperclassmen, directly accelerating student performance.
* Initiated the PhD Student Committee to bridge communication gaps and collaborate directly with department faculty to execute the Annual PhD Research Symposium.

positions.title: Graduate Research Assistant
positions.description:
As a graduate research assistant, I focused on building the high-throughput software and image processing pipelines needed to automate ophthalmic research. Writing over 12,000 lines of MATLAB code, I built computer vision algorithms that turned grueling manual processes into automated ones (including a lens segmentation tool that cut data analysis time by 80%, and a novel 3D algorithm that crunched through more than 160,000 in-vivo OCT images to validate previously unreachable clinical data).

I also developed practical software that solves workflow bottlenecks. I designed an end-to-end data visualization desktop application used daily by my team, built automated tools to process 220,000 raw frames for wavefront reconstruction, and created a custom file-conversion executable that became the foundation for all downstream laboratory data. Our findings were highly collaborative, scaling to clinical partners in Spain and India, and resulting in 6 peer-reviewed papers and over 20 global conference presentations.

positions.description:

positions.title: Research Associate
positions.description:

used for: image viewing, image registration, boundary detection, and statistical image
analyses.
• Trained users and created user manuals for software developed

positions.title: Undergraduate Research Assistant
positions.description:
• Developed a MATLAB imaging application for imaging the retinal nerve fiber layer
(RNFL) of rat retinas.
    * Developed user-friendly interface that allowed experiment parameters to be
previewed, analyzed, and stored
    * Created interface for controlling CCD camera and voltage retarder
    * Integrated control of a CCD camera and voltage retarder into a user-friendly
interface

honors.title: Best Phd Student Presentation (Inaugural Research Day)
honors.description: This was awarded for a presentation competition that mimicked a "Three-Minute-Thesis (3MT)" style.  I was tasked with condensing the essence of my research to a 3-minute presentation.
honors.issuer: Issued by University of Miami, College of Engineering · Sep 2018

honors.title: Alpha Eta Mu Beta Induction
honors.description:
I was initially offered membership to this honor society during the course of my undergraduate career. 
 However, I officially became a member  as a graduate student in 2017.
honors.issuer: Issued by Alpha Eta Mu Beta · Mar 2017

I joined Team Rubicon post hurricane Dorian to aid the Bahamas in their rebuild effort.
